item.title: A press release by Ministry of External Affairs, says, External Affairs Minister meets President of Guyana on the sidelines of CHOGM in Antigua and Ba...
item.description:
A press release by Ministry of External Affairs, says,
External Affairs Minister meets President of Guyana on the sidelines of CHOGM in Antigua and Barbuda (November 04, 2026)

EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar met H.E. Dr. Mohamed Irfaan Ali, President of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana, on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda today.

2. The two leaders reviewed the entire gamut of India-Guyana bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, energy, agriculture, infrastructure development, digital technology and capacity building.

3. During the meeting, the following three agreements were signed between the two countries:

a) Supply and Installation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Manufacturing Projects.

b) Grant Assistance for Implementation of Quick Impact Projects (QIPs).

c) Cooperation in the Field of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and the Functioning of a Unified Payments Interface (UPI)-like System in Guyana.

4. EAM also announced India’s extension of a US$500 million new Line of Credit to Guyana to support its development priorities and infrastructure projects. India has already completed several development projects in Guyana, and the new Line of Credit will further strengthen the development partnership between the two countries.

5. India and Guyana share longstanding and close relations, rooted in historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. As Global South partners and members of the Commonwealth, India and Guyana continue to work together to strengthen their multifaceted cooperation and advance shared priorities for development and prosperity."

item.description:
STORY | Air quality very poor in Delhi

Delhi's air quality was recorded in the 'very poor' category on Thursday, with the Air Quality Index settling at 367, according to the Central Pollution Control Board.

Alipur recorded the worst air quality at 427, falling in the 'severe' category.

An AQI between zero and 50 is classified as good, 51 and 100 as satisfactory, 101 and 200 as moderate, 201 and 300 as poor, 301 and 400 as very poor, and 401 and 500 as severe.

The minimum temperature at Safdarjung, Delhi's primary weather station, settled at 16.4 degrees Celsius on Thursday, 1.1 degrees above the season's average, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The maximum temperature is likely to hover around 28 degrees Celsius.

item.title: 🇨🇴 🚨 COLOMBIA: NATIONAL CIVIL REGISTRY ALLEGEDLY BREACHED, 41.4M CITIZEN RECORDS FOR SALE A threat actor using the alias "GordonFreeman1" cla...
item.description:
🇨🇴 🚨 COLOMBIA: NATIONAL CIVIL REGISTRY ALLEGEDLY BREACHED, 41.4M CITIZEN RECORDS FOR SALE

A threat actor using the alias "GordonFreeman1" claims on a dark web forum to be selling 41,415,693 records (about 1.45TB) allegedly taken from Colombia's National Civil Registry (Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil), the body that runs national ID and elections.

The actor alleges the data includes:
* Full names
* National ID document numbers, issue dates and status
* Dates and places of birth

The actor says access came through a vulnerable API, is asking $20,000, and is also offering a custom lookup API built on the data. The listing claims records of political leaders and celebrities are included. None of this has been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If genuine, this would cover most of Colombia's population. ID numbers paired with birth data are a ready kit for identity fraud, account takeover and targeted phishing, and a lookup API makes abuse trivial. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

STORY | Incredible to see blue wave: NYC Mayor Mamdani on Democrats' sweeping mid-term polls

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Wednesday said that the results of the mid-term elections are a “referendum” on politicians telling working people that their needs were unrealistic, and it was “incredible” to see the sweeping victories registered by Democrats in the House and Senate.

“It was incredible to see the blue wave,” Mamdani said at a press conference.

He was referring to the sweeping wins across the country registered by the Democratic Party in Tuesday’s mid-term elections that have given them control of the House and Senate and delivered a stunning rebuke to President Donald Trump and the policies of the Republican Party.

Mamdani said the result was a referendum on politics at large across America.

“This referendum was on politicians telling working people that their needs were unrealistic, while those same politicians were willing to do whatever it is that the wealthiest people in the country would ask them to do. And I think this election is also a referendum on (Vice President) J D Vance asking for two more years to deliver on the things that Americans cannot afford even another day of delay on,” he said.

item.title: STORY | Trump admits war in Iran, oil prices led to poll loss; but says would 'do it again' US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it was “large...
item.description:
STORY | Trump admits war in Iran, oil prices led to poll loss; but says would 'do it again'

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it was “largely true” that the war in Iran cost the Republicans heavy losses in the midterm election but struck a defiant note, saying he would do it again as it was the “only answer” in the “long term”.

"Well, I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term," Trump told reporters when asked about Vice President J D Vance’s remarks that the Iran war led to Republican losses in the election.

"But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he said.

The president insisted that the US would have done nothing different as far as the war was concerned.

"But I can tell you that as far as that war is concerned, I would have done nothing different. We've totally broken their military. The navy's gone. Their air force is gone. Their anti-aircraft is gone," Trump said.

“The Iran thing, we had to do, and we continue to do it. We have tremendous oil flowing out of the Hormuz Strait now. At the beginning, there was none. And, probably, that's the primary reason – the price, not the war, the price (of oil),” Trump said.

The president also said that he was not considering replacing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, despite public dissatisfaction with the war with Iran.

Hegseth is “doing a great job", he said.

Vice President JD Vance, often eyed as Trump's likely successor at the White House, blamed the president's war in Iran for Republicans' midterm wipeout.

(Report by Sagar Kulkarni /PTI)

item.title: 🇮🇩 INDONESIA: HACKTIVIST-STYLE POST CLAIMS TO LEAK DATA ON INDONESIAN NATIONAL POLICE (POLRI) OFFICERS A threat actor on a dark web forum has po...
item.description:
🇮🇩 INDONESIA: HACKTIVIST-STYLE POST CLAIMS TO LEAK DATA ON INDONESIAN NATIONAL POLICE (POLRI) OFFICERS

A threat actor on a dark web forum has posted what it claims is data on "some members" of Indonesia's National Police (Polri), framed as a protest against the government and police.

According to the post:
* A free code-block sample of what the actor calls police officer records
* Visible rows appear to include names, ranks, unit labels such as criminal investigation (Reskrim), phone numbers and ID-style numbers
* The listing also refers to emails and usernames, which the capture does not show
* No record count is given

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The post mixes a protest photo and taunting text with a data sample, which fits hacktivist messaging aimed at Indonesian authorities. A separate small "Polri" archive surfaced on another forum last week, so these may be recycled or partial datasets rather than a fresh compromise. If the records are authentic, exposed officer names and phone numbers raise the risk of doxxing, harassment, impersonation and targeted phishing against police personnel. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach of Polri systems.

Hence, Congress, which is losing its ground everywhere, has now become dependent on parties like AAP and other regional entities. As for Mr Kharge's claim that Congress lost in Gujarat and other states because of AAP, it is simply a case of 'a bad workman blaming his tools' (naach na aave aangan tedha). NIKKE's PC launcher became a malware delivery route through compromised official CDN scripts.

Researcher MotherSphere documents a remote-control agent with command execution, file access and credential-stealing capabilities. Independent analysis of two altered scripts confirmed the malicious loader.

* The official NIKKE notice reports client fixes, with the impact still under investigation.
* The researcher's November 4 update says all four affected scripts were clean on four checked CDN servers at 11:20 GMT.
* Previously infected PCs and cached malicious files still require investigation. Clean server files do not establish that affected computers are clean.

The number of infected players and any actual credential or cryptocurrency theft remain unknown. No evidence establishes that other games were affected.

🇵🇭 🚨 PHILIPPINES: HACKERS LEAK ~10GB FROM OFFICE OF THE VICE PRESIDENT

A threat actor calling itself "DeathNoteHackers" has published a roughly 10GB archive it claims was stolen from the Office of the Vice President (OVP) of the Philippines.

The actor claims:
• ~10GB of PDF documents, labeled "Office of the Vice President [Scheduler]"
• Files tied to the OVP's scheduling and administrative operations
• The leak is part of a broader campaign against government budget practices
• The archive is being spread through public file-sharing links

The claim has not been independently verified, and the OVP has not commented.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Unverified leak claim. If authentic, schedule and administrative files could expose officials' movements, internal workflows and staff PII, raising both physical-security and phishing risks. Government staff should expect targeted lures referencing the leak.

item.description:
🇺🇸 🚨 HILTON: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS "CENTRAL SERVER" BREACH, DEMANDS 2 BTC

A threat actor on a dark web forum claims to have breached a central server of Hilton, the global hotel chain, and is extorting the company.

The actor claims:
• Data on "all Hilton Hotels customers" plus other internal data
• CSV files and screenshots shared as proof
• A 10-day deadline to pay 2 BTC to have the data deleted
• Otherwise the full database will be sold publicly for 0.5 BTC

The claim has not been independently verified, and Hilton has not commented.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Unverified extortion claim, NOT confirmation of a breach. "All customers" claims against major brands are often exaggerated, and the low resale price is a caution flag. If authentic, guest PII could fuel targeted phishing and booking scams, so Hilton Honors members should watch for fake reservation or loyalty-points emails.

The Brain Cipher ransomware group has added FBC (fbc[.]ca), a Canada-wide tax and financial-services firm for small businesses and farmers, to its data-leak site.

The gang claims to hold about 174,000 files totaling more than 73 GB, including tax returns, financial statements, correspondence, signatures and bank information tied to more than 1,200 farm and individual clients.

FBC says it serves more than 20,000 small-business and farm members and files tens of thousands of tax returns a year. If genuine, a leak of that scale would expose sensitive tax and banking data for Canadian farmers and SMEs and create a clear phishing and fraud risk. We assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

item.description:
🇬🇧 🚨 UNILEVER NAMED BY "WHITEARMOR" EXTORTION GROUP

WhiteArmor, the data-extortion crew that surfaced in late October, has added Unilever, the London-headquartered consumer goods giant behind more than 400 brands, to its leak site.

The listing went up on November 4. So far the group has not publicly detailed what it claims to hold, how much data is involved, or what it is demanding.

The claim has not been independently verified, and Unilever has not publicly confirmed a cyber incident.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
WhiteArmor has spent its first two weeks naming big brands (Whirlpool, Hisense, J.B. Hunt, Ryder, KuCoin), but none of its claims has been matched to an official breach notice so far, and some may be inflated or recycled. Unilever was also named in an unproven 2024 hacktivist claim. Suppliers and partners should stay alert for phishing or invoice fraud using Unilever branding. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Prime Minister, on Latin America, Europe and the push toward isolation:

"Spain will always be there to open Europe's doors to you, together with our Portuguese brothers."

"Today I want to invite our friends, brothers and sisters in Latin America and the Caribbean to follow the example of Canada and tighten their ties with Europe, so that both regions build a stronger, more ambitious alliance with greater weight in the world."

"Too many countries seem to have reached the same unfortunate conclusion: that to protect yourself you have to close up, close borders, raise barriers, reduce cooperation and see the rest of the world as a threat rather than an opportunity."

"I believe we must do exactly the opposite. Against those who close themselves off, we must open up. Against those who build walls, we must build alliances. And against those who fuel war, we must be sowers of peace."

"We don't want a world of countries that are increasingly alone. We want a world of countries that are increasingly united."

item.title: Beget says a destructive cyberattack wiped its VPS, S3 and Kubernetes data. The Russian hosting provider says attackers reached its infrastructure man...
item.description:
Beget says a destructive cyberattack wiped its VPS, S3 and Kubernetes data.

The Russian hosting provider says attackers reached its infrastructure management systems and ran deletion scripts overnight November 1–2.

* Binary VPS backups were also lost.
* File-level backups survived, but access depends on restoring the supporting infrastructure.
* More than 1,000 servers require manual inspection before services can fully return.

Beget's November 4 update reports the first shared-hosting websites back online. That is partial recovery, not confirmation that cloud data has been restored.

An affected publisher independently confirms its own outage. The full loss figures, entry point and attacker identity remain unverified outside Beget.

https://t.me/beget_official/573
https://beget.com/ru
